instruction: Left arm: lift the blue holed block by its handle and hold it up. Right arm: put the red peg into the block's hole and let go of it, then move away. The left arm keeps holding the block.

outcome.real_measurement: In the hole: the peg's bottom centre within 8 mm of the hole axis (block frame) at every judged step (hole clearance 5 mm per side). Real world: pose tracking of peg and block.
Inserted: the peg's bottom centre within 1 cm of the hole floor (>= 3.4 cm of the 4.4 cm hole) at every judged step. Real world: pose tracking / depth gauge mark on the peg.
Aligned: peg axis within 15 deg of the hole axis (a peg standing in the hole leans at most ~13 deg). Real world: pose tracking.
Supported by the block: peg-block contact impulse > 0 in every judged step.
The peg does not touch the table.
Held by the left arm: left robot-block contact impulse > 0 in every judged step. Real world: left gripper current / F-T.
The block is off the table (no table-block contact in the judged window).
Held up: the block's lowest corner >= 1.5 cm above the table at every judged step.

Commanded vs actual opening (v3.2, E24c fix 3): for every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of a judged object, measured opening minus the free-space opening of its current gripper command <= 5 mm at every judged step (a gripper still closing on, or propped open by, something fails). Real world: gripper encoder vs command.

Consequence test after the judged window (protocol v3.1/v3.2): every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of the peg retracts its TCP 3 cm along its approach axis in 0.5 s with its last gripper command unchanged, then holds 0.5 s; the peg must move <= 1 cm. Real world: same motion, tracked pose.
Settled: the fastest bounding-box corner of every judged object moves <= 2 cm/s at every judged step, speed from positions (v3.2, E24c fix 1). Real world: frame differencing of the tracked pose.
Stays put: the block centre moves <= 2 mm over the judged window. Real world: tracked pose, 1 s.
Stays put: the peg centre moves <= 2 mm over the judged window. Real world: tracked pose, 1 s.

counterexamples.name: expert
counterexamples.description: positive control: left lifts the block 3.5 cm and holds it; right picks the peg, inserts it along the hole axis to 4 mm above the floor, opens, backs off, goes home

counterexamples.name: hold_peg
counterexamples.description: as the expert, but the right arm never opens (peg inside the hole, still in its gripper)

counterexamples.name: peg_at_entrance
counterexamples.description: the right arm holds the peg with its bottom 1 cm above the hole mouth (not inserted)

counterexamples.name: block_on_table
counterexamples.description: the left arm never moves (block left on the table); the right arm inserts the peg, opens, backs off

source.protocol: v3 (veritask, unchanged) + imsim v3.2 signals (imsim/imsim/verify/v32.py): position-based speeds, all-link enclosure, retreat aftermath, commanded vs actual opening, 5 s settle cap
source.released_code_predicate: env info['success']: peg bottom centre within 8 mm of the hole axis and within 12 mm of the hole floor at the evaluated step (no release, no settle, nothing about the block being held)

notes: Release over the peg only (contact with every robot link + all-link enclosure); the block is NOT released (it must be held by the left arm: arm0_block contact in every judged step, no table contact, >= 1.5 cm up). The retreat aftermath moves only arms whose gripper is within 3 cm of the PEG (recorder aftermath=['peg']); the left arm stays under hold A. Quiescence over block and peg.
